ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 cancellation fee; no refund or voucher is due. Close the dispute and inform the rider that Grace extends only while the driver is en route to the pickup, not after the vehicle has arrived and the rider has been given the statutory wait.
ruling.reasoning:
The cancellation was made by the driver, so the fee can only arise through NS-0's driver-side branch, and the driver's stated ground is rider no-show [F4]. NS-1 therefore governs: the fee stands only if (i) arrival was confirmed by the driver's "I'm Here" tap (or an automatic arrival confirmation), (ii) the driver was at the pickup point at that moment, and (iii) the driver then waited continuously at the pickup for more than 3 minutes until cancelling [F6].

On (i) and (ii), the system record shows a driver tap at 18:24:35 and a GPS position 41 m from the pickup at that instant, inside the 200 m data-layer radius (closest approach overall 38 m) [F6][F1]. These two elements are met and are not seriously disputed on either side [F6].

On (iii), NS-1 measures the continuous wait from the arrival confirmation — here the tap — not from the earlier moment the driver first entered the radius [F6][F2]. The tap was at 18:24:35 and the cancellation at 18:28:25, giving 230 seconds (3 min 50 s) of continuous presence inside the radius after the tap; the threshold is 180 seconds [F6][F4][F2]. The trace confirms the samples run from the arrival confirmation to the cancellation with no gap beyond the hole threshold, and the driver was stationary at a single point 41 m from the pickup from 18:24:15 until the cancellation, so the continuity is proved by samples rather than inferred across a hole [F2][F3][F4]. The requirement is therefore satisfied [F6][F4].

The counter-argument that the clock should start at the first entry into the radius (18:22:45, cumulative 5 min 15 s within 200 m) would only lengthen the wait, not shorten it, and the argument that 3 min 50 s is "barely" over the line does not change the outcome: the clause's only threshold is "more than 3 minutes", and 3 min 50 s clears it [F2][F5][F6]. The driver's post-trip statement claiming "more than 4 minutes" of waiting and two calls is a statement, not the operative record, and where it differs from the timeline it does not displace it; even disregarding it entirely, the tap-to-cancel window of 3 min 50 s independently satisfies NS-1(iii), so the overstatement is immaterial [F13][F6][F4].

The rider's message asking for "2 more minutes" at 18:25 is a request for grace, not an acknowledgement that any NS-1 element fails, and it does not extend the rider's protected window: NS-1 sets the no-show threshold at more than 3 minutes of post-arrival waiting, which the driver gave [F10][F6][F4]. Heavy rain (18.5 mm) and slow traffic on Maxwell Road do not alter the analysis: no traffic exception is needed because this is not a route-deviation case, and NS-8 (a driver late beyond ETA) is not a citable rule and in any event concerns the driver not arriving, not the rider not appearing [F16][F14].

Because all three NS-1 elements hold, NS-2's refund trigger is not reached and the $6.61 cancellation fee is properly due [F6][F7]. The fee is the published figure for a rider no-show and no surge applied, so the amount is unmodified [F7][F8]. NS-7 is procedural: it would fix the voucher form and the 30-day window had a refund been owed, but no refund is owed, so it changes nothing here [F7].

Profile facts do not decide the case. The driver's 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days cannot support an account flag because RD-6 is conditioned on a finding against the driver under RD-2 or a recorded RD-1 breach, neither of which exists here, and the rider advocate withdrew that claim; the rider's own clean record likewise carries no weight [F18][F17].

Safety screen: I read all three chat messages, the driver's written statement and the complaint [F9][F10][F11][F13]. The messages concern arrival, a request for two minutes and a cancellation announcement; the complaint is about the fee. Nothing in them is a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark, abuse or dangerous-driving allegation, so the screen is "none" [F9][F10][F11][F13]. Evidence is sufficient: the chat is complete with every message timestamped, the GPS trace covers the wait without a hole, and every element the ruling needs is settled by record rather than by inference [F12][F2][F6][F4].

rejected_claims.reason: The premise that NS-1(iii) fails is wrong: the tap at 18:24:35 and cancellation at 18:28:25 give 3 min 50 s (230 s) of continuous presence inside the 200 m radius after the driver's own arrival confirmation, exceeding the 180 s threshold [F6][F4][F2]. The claimant is correct that the clock runs from the tap, which is exactly why NS-1(iii) is satisfied, not defeated [F6][NS-1].

NS-1(ii) is satisfied (41 m at the tap) and so is NS-1(iii) (230 s > 180 s from the tap to cancellation), so not all three elements fail and NS-2's full-refund trigger is never reached; the $6.61 stands [F6][F7][NS-2].

The rider's request for two more minutes does not extend the statutory window; the driver gave more than the 3 minutes NS-1 requires after arrival confirmation before cancelling, so the request does not convert a valid no-show charge into an invalid one [F10][F6][F4][NS-1].

Conceded as far as it goes — the chat is complete and the system timeline governs over the driver's post-hoc statement — but the system timeline here supports the fee: the tap-to-cancel window of 3 min 50 s independently satisfies NS-1(iii), so the driver's overstatement of his wait is immaterial [F12][F13][F6][F4][NS-1].
NS-7 only governs the form and timing of a refund if one is owed; no refund is owed because every NS-1 element is met, so no $6.61 voucher is payable [F7][F6][NS-7].

Withdrawn by the claimant and independently inapplicable: RD-6 requires a finding against the driver under RD-2 or a recorded RD-1 breach, and this case involves no route deviation and no refund, so the driver's prior no-show disputes cannot support an account flag here [F18][F7][RD-6].

The driver's profile (3.6 years, 4.92 rating, 1244 trips) cannot decide the case; profile facts never decide alone, and the ruling rests on the recorded tap, GPS position and wait window, not on the driver's record [F18][NS-1].
